title: Syracuse Police Department ALPR Policy 427
summary: Published Syracuse Police Department policy governing ALPR capture, access, retention, auditing, reporting, and external release as of July 28, 2026.

evidence.claim: Stored ALPR data has a 30-day baseline retention period, with a three-month preservation extension available for felony investigations and longer preservation for evidence, discovery, or other lawful production obligations.

Access requires a protected system capable of documenting access by name/date/time; members must provide call type, justification, and associated DR number; Compliance conducts quarterly internal audits.

External law-enforcement/prosecutorial requests require a written request with agency, requester, purpose, and case/report number plus Support Services Bureau Chief or designee approval; vendor sharing is prohibited, and immigration-enforcement sharing with ICE/DHS is prohibited absent judicial or court order.

data.question: What public evidence now establishes Syracuse's Axon ALPR deployment state and operational control model without conflating announced policy with technical configuration?
data.method: Reconciled the current canonical Syracuse transition packet with Syracuse Police Department Policy 427, the public Axon transparency portal surface, and July 29, 2026 independent reporting based on SPD confirmation.
data.framework: Keep Flock and Axon as separate network eras; distinguish written policy, technical configuration, observed activity, and unresolved migration.
data.scope: Syracuse Police Department ALPR policy and initial Axon stationary-reader activation state through July 29, 2026.
findings: SPD Policy 427 was published July 28, 2026 and governs both mobile and stationary ALPR use.

Policy 427 sets a 30-day baseline retention period; felony-investigation data may be preserved for an additional three months, with longer preservation when evidentiary/discovery/legal obligations apply.
Policy 427 requires logged access and a call type, justification, and DR number for queries, plus quarterly Compliance audits.

Policy 427 allows controlled external law-enforcement/prosecutorial sharing by written request and approval, prohibits vendor sharing, and prohibits ICE/DHS immigration-enforcement sharing absent judicial or court order.
Central Current reported SPD confirmed 14 of 26 new stationary Axon readers were installed and activated at 7:00 a.m. July 27, 2026; 12 remained awaiting installation.

The public Axon transparency portal existed when the policy/activation state was reported, but policy publication and portal availability do not establish that all stated technical controls are enforced.
conclusions: Syracuse's Axon era is no longer merely planned: a partial stationary-reader deployment was active by July 27, 2026.
The published control model is materially more specific than the prior unresolved state, but it is a policy baseline rather than proof of implementation.
The 'closed-system' target remains unresolved because the written policy expressly allows some external sharing and native configuration/audit evidence has not yet been recovered.
No Flock-to-Axon migration edge should be created from this evidence.
recommendations: Recover the executed Axon contract/procurement package and product schedule.
Recover the final 26-reader inventory with serials, locations, ownership, installation/activation timestamps, and status.
Recover native Axon access/audit logs, role assignments, sharing settings, regional Crime Analysis Center agreement, retention configuration, and hotlist configuration.
Compare policy-required quarterly audits and transparency reports with native logs before resolving the closed-system target.
Continue to test Flock-to-Axon migration only with native records.
counterarguments: A published no-vendor-sharing rule does not establish that Axon technically cannot access metadata or service telemetry; the policy is the controlling public statement, not a configuration export.
The initial 14/26 activation count does not prove the remaining 12 were later installed or activated.
limitations: This pass did not recover the executed Axon contract, native configuration exports, serial inventory, or complete post-July deployment history.
unresolved: What are the final serial/location/activation records for all 26 Axon stationary readers?
What sharing agreement exists with the regional Crime Analysis Center and how is it configured?
Do production retention settings match Policy 427's 30-day baseline and preservation exceptions?
Which users/roles can query, share, preserve, or export ALPR data and what do quarterly audit logs show?
Did any Flock hotlists, user identities, cases, historical reads, or other data migrate into Axon?
